title: Chapter 2 Quiz 5
description: A mixed review of Chapter 2. Say how sure you are before you check.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: A program checks whether a number is positive and prints a different message in each case. Which type of algorithm is this?
questions.explanation: A decision between two outcomes: conditional.

questions.question: Summing all the elements of an array is a task for an…
questions.explanation: We repeat the same addition for every element: a loop.

questions.question: Exploring every folder inside other folders is best described by a…
questions.explanation: Each folder contains the same kind of problem, only smaller.

questions.question: Match each term to its meaning.
right: Makes the locally optimal choice at each step
Finds the position of an element
questions.explanation: A review of the families and approaches.

questions.question: Which of these are **design approaches**?
questions.explanation: Top-down and bottom-up are design approaches. Greedy and sorting describe kinds of algorithm.

questions.question: A recursive algorithm solves a problem by calling itself on smaller sub-problems.
questions.explanation: That is the definition of recursion.

questions.assertion: Merge sort is a divide and conquer algorithm.
questions.reason: It splits the data into smaller parts, sorts them and combines the results.
questions.explanation: Both are true and the reason explains why merge sort is divide and conquer.

questions.question: Which approach solves the simplest sub-problems first and then combines them?
questions.explanation: Bottom-up builds the answer from the smallest pieces.
